newsitem.title: TAIWAN: FOCUS-Taiwan money rates soar on new stock rally.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Taiwan money rates soar on new stock rally.

text.p: Taiwan's interbank rate roared briefly above nine percent and closed at a 21-month peak on Tuesday despite central bank stabilisation efforts, as a frantic stock market siphoned funds from the banking system.

Dealers said the rates should begin to abate on Wednesday after the central bank, trying a novel approach, injected T$20 billion into the funds-strapped market by allowing a state-run bank to withdraw the amount to bolster overall liquidity.
The overnight interbank rate, capping a seven-session ascent, soared to a high of 9.125 percent before the central bank's injection eased it to 8.395 at Tuesday's close.
That close still surpassed Monday's 8.323 finish and marked the highest close since 8.523 on September 16, 1995.
The central bank endorses a 5.0-5.5 percent "target zone".
The 30-day commercial paper rose to 8.00-8.75 percent against 7.50-7.75.
Dealers said the rates skyrocketed on a torrent of funds flowing out of the banking system into a red-hot bourse that has gained almost 300 points or three percent since June 16.
The overnight rate stood at 5.977 percent on June 16.

The stock index slipped 6.95 points or 0.08 percent to 8,918.17 on Tuesday, on stabilising turnover of T$169.38 billion (US$6.1 billion) -- well below an all-time high T$251 billion set on June 19 at the outset of the latest rally.
Dealers said the central bank's late injection on Tuesday meant the bank intended to guide money rates downward regardless of what happened in the stock market.

"The central bank injection means the rates have reached the upper limit of the bank's tolerance," said one dealer. "The rates for the rest of the week should fall gradually, and I do not rule out a sharper descent starting next week."

The central bank, through its unprecedented "closed" injection, allowed state-run Taiwan Cooperative Bank to make the T$20 billion withdrawal to offer an interest rate of eight percent -- a full percentage point below the market norm.
"The low offer by the Taiwan Cooperative Bank was probably guided by the central bank," said another dealer.

Just as the money market closed on Tuesday, the central bank confirmed it would continue to tinker with liquidity through issues of negotiable certificates of deposit, but reiterated that it would not inject funds through open-market operations.
Central bank business director Lee Sheng-yen added the bank did not plan to cut reserve requirements because "the current tight liquidity will not last long."
In the bond market, the benchmark 10-year 86/4 bond yield was at 5.8600 percent against Monday's 5.8590-8600.
